Laboratory data reveal markedly elevated LDL‑C and total cholesterol, borderline creatinine, and low CO₂, while no blood pressure or eGFR values are recorded. Integrating demographic risk, the lipid abnormality emerges as the most probable active diagnosis, followed by likely untreated hypertension and silent coronary atherosclerosis. Secondary considerations (OSA, early CKD, PAD, mood disorder, anemia work‑up, endocrine causes) are supported by the same risk profile and the unexplained laboratory findings.
